entities.summary:
Count János Forgách de Ghymes et Gács (1878-1935) was a Hungarian diplomat of Austro-Hungarian origin who played a pivotal role during World War I and the July Crisis. He served as an ambassador to several European countries, including Austria-Hungary, Germany, and Italy. Forgách was instrumental in negotiating the Treaty of Saint-Germain-en-Laye, which officially ended World War I and led to the dissolution of the Austro-Hungarian Empire. His diplomatic efforts also contributed to the reorganization of Eastern Europe after the war.

Forgách's significance extends beyond his diplomatic career, as he was a key figure in the Hungarian Red Cross and a vocal advocate for Hungarian independence during the war. His experiences during this period had a lasting impact on his life and work, shaping his views on international relations and diplomacy.

Despite his prominent role in Hungarian history, Forgách remains a relatively unknown figure outside of Hungary, and his legacy is slowly being rediscovered by historians and scholars.

In 1935, Forgách passed away on September 25, at the age of 57, leaving behind a legacy of diplomatic acumen and a commitment to Hungarian independence that continues to inspire scholars and policymakers today.

Count János Forgách de Ghymes et Gács was a prominent Austro-Hungarian diplomat of Hungarian origin who played a pivotal role during World War I and the July Crisis.

Born on October 24, 1870, in Halič, Ukraine, Forgách served as the Austrian Ambassador to Italy from 1909 until his death in 1935. He was known for his diplomatic skills and strategic thinking, which helped navigate complex international relationships during a tumultuous period in European history.

Forgách's significance lies in his ability to maintain relations with various nations, including Italy, Germany, and the United Kingdom, despite the rising tensions leading up to the war. His efforts to prevent conflict and promote peace were instrumental in shaping the course of events during the July Crisis.

As a key figure in Austro-Hungarian diplomacy, Forgách's legacy extends beyond his own time, influencing international relations and diplomatic practices for generations to come.

The phrase 'in the shadow of the eagle' ('a gyepen árnyékában') encapsulates Forgách's life and work, symbolizing his dedication to Austria-Hungary's interests despite facing significant challenges from within and outside its borders.
